items.title: Howie Shear interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2014
items.q: So if you could be Jekyll and Hyde in the sense that two different people...

ctx.x: Do you think it’s harder for a young player today to find an original sound because they have so much codified material to draw from.

Well you have to realize that the codified material is half of it, and the other half is sort of the primal part of you, the creative part of you that wants to take that vocabulary or that lexicon and then play it in a very non-academic way. So if you could be Jekyll and Hyde in the sense that two different people, in order to get across what you want to get across. But yeah, there’s a lot of players out there that forget about that other half, they’re very academic about it and they say well the book says to…
So are there wrong notes in improvising?
